pairs.question: Noxia tu coniux magis an draco perfidus ille?
pairs.answer: Perfidus ille draco, sed tu quoque noxia coniux.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (is the wife more guilty, or the serpent?) answered by the poet in the immediately following verse. Question and answer are adjacent verses; the question is self-contained, naming both coniux and draco. No scaffolding embedded in these two lines. Answer ends at its own full stop (the verse-end); what follows ('Pro dolor!...') begins a new exclamation.

pairs.question: Cur tria dona tamen?
pairs.answer: Quoniam spes maxima vitae est Hunc numerum confessa fides, et tempora summus Cernens cuncta Deus, praesentia, prisca, futura, Semper adest semperque fuit semperque manebit In triplici virtute sui.
pairs.derivation: Authorial question on why three gifts (the magi's gold/frankincense/myrrh just described) answered by the poet with 'quoniam...'. The answer is the single sentence from 'Quoniam' to the first full stop after 'sui'; the inline every-5-lines verse number '100' dangling before 'In triplici' is scaffolding and stripped. What follows the cut is the editorial dash and a new sentence ('— Tunc caelitus illi / Per somnum moniti...'). 'Hunc numerum' (= three) is grounded by 'tria' in the question, so the pair is self-contained.
